alyssa: Quick sync — customers pushed back on retention options and BYOK semantics in last week's pilot ask. Need a short, concrete roadmap we can show sales/legal. Can we align on minimal launch criteria and a conservative timeline? @tom @vivian @raj
tom: From eng side, minimal launch should be: 1) immutable audit snapshots for 90d (hash + signed manifest), 2) BYOK handshake that supports single-key per-tenant and rotation-with-rollback, 3) export API (ndjson) and an index layout migration plan. Anything else mandatory?
vivian: SOC2 and ISO customers require proof of integrity and access logs. For SOC2 we also need isolation of evidence exports and retention policy metadata in the export. Legal wants legal-hold support that prevents deletion regardless of retention TTL.
raj: Storage cost is the biggest constraint for long tails. Recommend phased retention caps per tier: standard enterprise = 1y (hot/warm/cold tiers), extended = add-on for 3y and 7y. Also need clear egress cost obligations if customers request full export.
alyssa: Proposal: Launch pillars = (A) Core tamper-evidence + snapshot signing, (B) BYOK basic handshake + rotation API, (C) Search SLA for hot window + simple export. Target pilot customers only get 1y default, with extended retention gated behind billing/contract. Sound reasonable?
tom: Yes. Engineering acceptance criteria I will use: - snapshots generated at daily cadence, signed by timestamping service, manifests stored immutably; - BYOK handshake API returns key-id and attestation; - search P95 (0-30d) <= 350ms; - fallback path that serves degraded results if index migration in progress.
vivian: For audit acceptance I'll add: signed manifests, retention metadata in export, access log bundling, and a procedure for key compromise (revoke + re-encrypt path). Legal requests: language for SLAs and egress liability + ability to escrow keys to third party on demand. legal-bot: New doc template created: "enterprise-retention-sla-template". Link: https://docs.redwood.com/retention-sla-template
raj: Ops note: cold tier retrieval can't be <24h without serious infra cost. For extended retention we should plan an async retrieval job and charge premium SLA. We'll document retrieval SLAs per tier.
alyssa: Timeline draft: Week 0-2 -> design + acceptance criteria; Week 3-6 -> implement snapshots + BYOK handshake; Week 7-9 -> search SLA tuning + export endpoints; Week 10 -> SOC2 pilot kickoff. This assumes no major infra blockers. Any red flags?
tom: Might need extra ops support for migration scripts; add 2-week buffer if migrations involve reindexing. Also need feature flags per-tenant.
vivian: I'll draft the audit acceptance checklist and run it by security. Also propose a small review board for pilot customers: security + legal + product before enabling BYOK.
raj: I'll model cost impact for 1y vs 3y vs 7y (storage + retrieval + egress) and attach numbers to the pricing add-on.
alyssa: Action items: tom -> eng tickets + timeline update; vivian -> audit checklist + review board invite; raj -> cost model + pricing bullets; legal-bot -> SLA template link above. Target to present a one-pager to sales on Monday. If no objections, I'll lock this plan today.
vivian: No objections. Will prep slides.
tom: OK. Creating JIRA: INF-13021 enterprise-retention-launch. ops-bot: Created INF-13021 assigned tom, vivian, raj. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-13021
alyssa: Thanks everyone. End of thread.
